reference_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT o.order_id
FROM orders o
JOIN order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = l.product_id
WHERE p.brand = 'Basswell'
  AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-06 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-07 00:00:00'
alternatives: SELECT o.order_id FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = l.product_id WHERE p.brand = 'Basswell' AND CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) = DATE '2025-03-06' GROUP BY o.order_id

SELECT DISTINCT l.order_id FROM order_lines l JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = l.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = l.product_id AND p.brand = 'Basswell' WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-06 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-07 00:00:00'
SELECT DISTINCT s.order_id FROM sales s JOIN products p ON p.product_id = s.product_id WHERE p.brand = 'Basswell' AND s.order_date = DATE '2025-03-06'

other_way.sql: SELECT o.order_id FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = l.product_id WHERE p.brand = 'Basswell' AND CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) = DATE '2025-03-06' GROUP BY o.order_id
other_way.tradeoff: GROUP BY order_id also gives each order once, but DISTINCT says more plainly that only the list is wanted.
